entries.title: 2 Chronicles 32:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 Sennacherib invading Judah, Hezekiah fortifies himself, and encourages his people. 9 Against the blasphemies of Sennacherib, Hezekiah and Isaiah pray. 21 An angel destroys the host of the Assyrians. 24 Hezekiah praying in his sickness, God gives him a sign of recovery. 25 He waxing proud, is humbled by God. 27 His wealth and works. 31 His error in the ambassage of Babylon. 32 He dying, Manasseh succeeds him.

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 32:12
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
Hath not. 31:1; 2Ki 18:4,22; Isa 36:7 taken away.This was artfully malicious: many of the people had sacrificed to Jehovah on high places, (ch. 31:1;) and Hezekiah had removed them, as incentives to idolatry. Hence Rabshakeh insinuates that by so doing he had offended Jehovah, deprived the people of their religious rights, and that, consequently, he could neither expect the blessing of God, nor the cooperation of the people.

Ye shall worship. De 12:13,14,26,27 one altar. 4:1; Ex 27:1-8; 30:1-6; 40:26-29; 1Ki 7:48
